gloss: old age; the later years of life

definitions.gloss: old age; the old-age period; senescence
definitions.explanation: The stage of life corresponding to old age, typically considered to begin around 65 and to continue through the end of life. Used in demography, psychology, medicine, and general writing as a clinical or formal way to refer to this life stage.

examples.japanese: {老年期|ろうねんき}の{健康|けんこう}について{考|かんが}える。
examples.english: To think about health in old age.

examples.japanese: {老年期|ろうねんき}になっても{学|まな}び{続|つづ}けたい。
examples.english: I want to keep learning even in old age.

examples.japanese: {老年期|ろうねんき}に{入|はい}ると、{生活|せいかつ}のペースを{見直|みなお}す{人|ひと}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: When people enter old age, many reconsider the pace of their daily life.

examples.japanese: {老年期|ろうねんき}の{認知機能|にんちきのう}の{変化|へんか}については、{近年|きんねん}{多|おお}くの{研究|けんきゅう}が{進|すす}められている。
examples.english: Much research has advanced in recent years on changes in cognitive function during old age.

notes:
Composed of {老年|ろうねん} (old age) and {期|き} (period, phase). The {-期|き} suffix is widely used to label life stages: {幼年期|ようねんき} (early childhood), {青年期|せいねんき} (youth), {壮年期|そうねんき} (prime of life), {老年期|ろうねんき} (old age).

REGISTER:
{老年期|ろうねんき} is formal and clinical. It is common in academic writing, public-health documents, insurance and pension materials, and news articles about aging. In everyday conversation, Japanese speakers are more likely to say {お{年寄|としよ}り} (elderly people) or {高齢|こうれい}, or refer simply to {年|とし}を{取|と}ってから (after getting on in years).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {老年期|ろうねんき}に{入|はい}る: to enter old age
- {老年期|ろうねんき}を{迎|むか}える: to reach old age
- {老年期|ろうねんき}の{健康|けんこう}: health in old age
- {老年期|ろうねんき}{うつ{病|びょう}}: depression in old age

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {高齢期|こうれいき}: the elderly stage of life — very close in meaning, often used interchangeably in public-health contexts
- {壮年期|そうねんき}: prime of life (roughly middle age) — the preceding life stage
- {老後|ろうご}: one's later years, retirement years — more colloquial and personal, focused on life after retirement
- {晩年|ばんねん}: one's final years — specifically the very end of life, often used retrospectively
